doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Subbing with Duke Ellington
summary: Ten days subbing for Sam Woodyard; Ellington's conducting confused him and he relied on Harry Carney and Ray Nance.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Oh, my the list goes on and on. You played with Ellington, and —
I was just a sub for Sammy, it was only ten days with Duke, I subbed for Sammy.
Now you made a comment that you felt you didn’t play good with Ellington ‘cause you were listening too hard.
No I didn’t play well with that thing, no, I didn’t play well at all with that. Especially when Duke was conducting. He goes like this you know. He looked like a knuckle ball

pitcher up there, you wonder when he’s going to let the band start coming in. I didn’t know what he was doing. When Harry Carney beat off the tempo, I sounded like a million bucks with those guys. You know, he’d just go one, two, three, four, and man in you go. But Duke was like, whew, like whirling dervish. I said what’s he doing? What’s he doing? He says don’t worry, Harry will get the tempo for him. And then Harry would bring me in. But if Harry wasn’t beating the time off I didn’t know what I was doing. Keeping my eye on Ray Nance you know. Ray goes bing — that’s his one — okay, here we go. But I was not successful with that band. I was successful with Woody. I did okay with Harry James.
